items.title: Noninvasive AI-based system translates brain signals into written text
items.excerpt: Researchers at Meta AI, Universite PSL and the Rothschild Foundation Hospital introduced a noninvasive brain-activity-to-text approach that decodes language from brain signals without surgery, a step toward accessible brain-computer interfaces.

items.title: Brain-inspired AI is capable of flexible planning and problem-solving while using far less energy
items.excerpt: Graz University of Technology researchers built a brain-inspired AI model that plans flexibly and solves complex problems while consuming significantly less energy than conventional neural networks.

items.title: Claude AI finds cryptography weaknesses human experts missed
items.excerpt: Anthropic reports that its Claude Mythos Preview model discovered previously unknown mathematical weaknesses in cryptographic algorithms that human researchers had overlooked.

items.title: Privacy risks from medical AI are greater than previously thought
items.excerpt: A new study shows sensitive individual health information can be extracted from medical AI models far more effectively than earlier research indicated, raising the stakes for diagnostic model privacy.

items.title: Is AI Reasoning Right for the Wrong Reasons?
items.excerpt: The idea that AI can 'reason' is more intuitive than ever, but the science is far from settled; researchers probe whether models reason or merely appear to.

items.title: Two research efforts gave AI the same open problem. Their papers were submitted three hours apart
items.excerpt: An MIT PhD student and two UC cryptographers used GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra in different ways to solve the same open cryptography problem, raising new questions about independent discovery and scientific credit.

items.title: Clinical chatbots are taking medicine by storm. Should doctors trust them?
items.excerpt: A Nature Medicine study from NYU Langone Health tested general vs. specialized clinical AI models on clinical questions, finding specialized clinical AI performed worse than general models.

items.title: AI tool predicts how DNA sequences switch on genes across different cell types
items.excerpt: Max Planck researchers built Corgi (Context-aware Regulatory Genomics Inference), a deep-learning tool that predicts how the genome behaves and switches on genes across different cell types.
